title.zh: 卷五十七 志第四十七 藝文一
title.raw: 卷五十七 志第四十七 藝文一 Volume 57 Treatises 53: The Arts 1

translations.literal: Arts and Letters 1
translations.idiomatic: Arts and Letters, Part 1

sentences.zh: 自《六經》焚於秦而復出於漢，其師傅之道中絕，而簡編脫亂訛缺，學者莫得其本真，於是諸儒章句之學興焉。

translations.literal: From the time the Six Classics were burned in Qin and reemerged in Han, the way of masters and teachers was cut off midway, the bamboo slips fell into disorder with errors and omissions, and scholars could not obtain their true originals; thereupon the Ru learning of chapter-and-verse commentary arose.
translations.idiomatic: After the Six Classics were burned in the Qin and revived in the Han, the transmission from the sages was broken midway; bamboo slips were disordered, marred by errors and lacunae, and scholars could no longer recover the authentic texts. It was then that Ru learning in the form of chapter-and-verse commentary arose.

sentences.zh: 其後傳註、箋解、義疏之流，轉相講述，而聖道粗明，然其為說固已不勝其繁矣。

translations.literal: Afterward the streams of transmitted commentaries, glosses, exegeses, and comprehensive elucidations turned to lecturing on one another in succession, and the sage's way was roughly clarified, yet the explanations had already become more than could be borne in their profusion.
translations.idiomatic: Later came successive traditions of transmitted commentaries, glosses, exegeses, and comprehensive elucidations, each lecturing upon the last, until the sage's way was at least broadly clarified—yet the body of interpretation had already grown unbearably vast.

sentences.zh: 至於上古三皇五帝以來世次，國家興滅終始，僭竊偽亂，史官備矣。

translations.literal: As for the sequence of ages from antiquity, the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors onward, the rise and fall and beginning and end of states, usurpation, pretense, and false disorder—the historiographers have recorded them fully.
translations.idiomatic: As for the succession of ages from the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors down, the rise and fall of states, usurpations and false regimes—the historiographers have long since set it all down.

sentences.zh: 而傳記、小說，外暨方言、地理、職官、氏族，皆出於史官之流也。

translations.literal: Biographies, minor tales, and beyond them dialect glossaries, geography, official posts, and clan lineages—all issued from the stream of historiographers.
translations.idiomatic: Biographies, anecdotal fiction, and beyond them regional glossaries, geography, official posts, and clan genealogies—all stemmed from the historiographic tradition.

sentences.zh: 自孔子在時，方脩明聖經以絀繆異，而老子著書論道德。

translations.literal: From the time Confucius was alive, he was just then clarifying the sage classics to restrain aberrant doctrines, while Laozi composed a book discussing the Way and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Already in Confucius's own day he was refining the sage classics to curb heterodox teachings, while Laozi wrote his book on the Way and virtue.

sentences.zh: 接乎周衰，戰國遊談放蕩之士，田駢、慎到、列、莊之徒，各極其辯；

translations.literal: Following upon the decline of Zhou, in the Warring States the roaming talkers and unrestrained scholars—Tian Pian, Shen Dao, Lie, Zhuang, and their kind—each carried disputation to its limit;
translations.idiomatic: With the Zhou in decline came the Warring States, when itinerant debaters and free spirits—Tian Pian, Shen Dao, Lie Yukou, Zhuang Zhou, and their like—each pushed argument to the extreme;

sentences.zh: 而孟軻、荀卿始專脩孔氏，以折異端。

translations.literal: while Meng Ke and Xun Qing first devoted themselves exclusively to cultivating the Kong school to refute heterodox teachings.
translations.idiomatic: while Mencius and Xunzi were the first to devote themselves wholly to the Kong tradition in order to refute the heterodox schools.

sentences.zh: 然諸子之論，各成一家，自前世皆存而不絕也。

translations.literal: Yet the discourses of the various masters each formed a school of its own, and from former ages onward all have been preserved without perishing.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the masters' teachings each formed its own school, and from antiquity onward all have been preserved without dying out.

sentences.zh: 夫王跡熄而《詩》亡，《離騷》作而文辭之士興。

translations.literal: When royal traces were extinguished the Odes perished; when the Li Sao was composed, men of literary craft arose.
translations.idiomatic: When the royal way faded the Odes ceased; with the composition of the Li Sao, writers of belles lettres arose.

sentences.zh: 歷代盛衰，文章與時高下。

translations.literal: Through successive ages in rise and decline, literature rose and fell with the times.
translations.idiomatic: Through each age's prosperity or decline, literary writing rose and fell with the times.

sentences.zh: 然其變態百出，不可窮極，何其多也。

translations.literal: Yet its transformations issued in a hundred forms, impossible to exhaust in the end—how very many they were.
translations.idiomatic: Yet its forms shifted in endless variety, beyond all reckoning—how vast their number.

sentences.zh: 自漢以來，史官列其名氏篇第，以為六藝、九種、七略；

translations.literal: From Han onward, historiographers listed authors' names and the sections and scrolls of their works, making the Six Arts, Nine Categories, and Seven Summaries;
translations.idiomatic: From the Han onward, court historiographers catalogued authors and titles under the Six Arts, Nine Categories, and Seven Summaries;

sentences.zh: 至唐始分為四類，曰經、史、子、集。

translations.literal: by Tang they were first divided into four categories, called Classics, Histories, Masters, and Collections.
translations.idiomatic: and only in the Tang were works first sorted into four divisions: Classics, Histories, Masters, and Collections.

sentences.zh: 而藏書之盛，莫盛於開元，其著錄者，五萬三千九百一十五卷，而唐之學者自為之書者，又二萬八千四百六十九卷。

translations.literal: As for the greatness of book collections, none surpassed the Kaiyuan era: those entered in the catalog numbered 53,915 scrolls, while books composed by Tang scholars themselves numbered another 28,469 scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: No age matched the Kaiyuan reign in the wealth of its libraries: 53,915 scrolls were catalogued, and Tang scholars' own writings added another 28,469 scrolls.

translations.literal: Alas, it may be called magnificent!
translations.idiomatic: Truly, what abundance!

sentences.zh: 《六經》之道，簡嚴易直而天人備，故其愈久而益明。

translations.literal: The way of the Six Classics is concise, severe, easy, and direct, and Heaven and man are complete in it; therefore the longer the time, the clearer it becomes.
translations.idiomatic: The way of the Six Classics is concise, austere, plain, and direct, embracing both Heaven and humanity; hence the longer they endure, the brighter they shine.

sentences.zh: 其余作者眾矣，質之聖人，或離或合。

translations.literal: The remaining authors are many; tested against the sages, they part or accord.
translations.idiomatic: All other authors are legion; weighed against the sages, they diverge or align.

sentences.zh: 然其精深閎博，各盡其術，而怪奇偉麗，往往震發於其間，此所以使好奇博愛者不能忘也。

translations.literal: Yet in profundity, refinement, breadth, and magnitude each exhausts his art, and the strange, marvelous, grand, and beautiful often burst forth dazzlingly among them—this is why those who love curiosity and broad learning cannot forget them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in depth and breadth each master exhausts his craft, and the strange, the grand, and the beautiful often flash forth among them—hence those who delight in learning cannot put them aside.

sentences.zh: 然雕零磨滅，亦不可勝數，豈其華文少實，不足以行遠歟？

translations.literal: Yet those carved away, scattered, and ground to extinction are also beyond counting—might it be that ornate language with little substance is insufficient to travel far?
translations.idiomatic: Yet works lost to decay are beyond numbering—perhaps florid style without solid content cannot endure?

sentences.zh: 而俚言俗說，猥有存者，亦其有幸不幸者歟？

translations.literal: Yet vulgar speech and common tales vulgarly have some that survive—is this also a matter of fortune and misfortune?
translations.idiomatic: Yet coarse tales and popular lore sometimes survive—is this too a matter of luck?

sentences.zh: 今著於篇，有其名而亡其書者，十蓋五六也，可不惜哉。

translations.literal: Now those entered in these pages: of those that have a name but whose book is lost, five or six in ten are so—is it not lamentable?
translations.idiomatic: Of the titles recorded here, five or six in ten are names whose texts no longer survive—a loss indeed worth mourning.

sentences.zh: 初，隋嘉則殿書三十七萬卷，至武德初，有書八萬卷，重復相糅。

translations.literal: At first, in Sui the Jiaze Hall held 370,000 scrolls of books; by the beginning of Wude there were 80,000 scrolls, mingled with duplicates.
translations.idiomatic: Originally the Sui Jiaze Hall held 370,000 scrolls; by the opening of the Wude era only 80,000 remained, many of them duplicates.

sentences.zh: 王世充平，得隋舊書八千余卷，太府卿宋遵貴監運東都，浮舟溯河，西致京師，經砥柱舟覆，盡亡其書。

translations.literal: When Wang Shichong was pacified, more than 8,000 scrolls of old Sui books were obtained; Grand Steward Song Zungui supervised their transport from the eastern capital, floating boats up the river west to the capital; passing the Zhiju rapids the boats capsized and all the books were lost.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Shichong's defeat, over 8,000 scrolls of Sui books were recovered; Grand Steward Song Zungui supervised their shipment from the eastern capital by boat upriver to the capital, but at the Zhiju rapids the boats capsized and every scroll was lost.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，魏征、虞世南、顏師古繼為秘書監，請購天下書，選五品以上子孫工書者為書手，繕寫藏於內庫，以宮人掌之。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era Wei Zheng, Yu Shinan, and Yan Shigu in succession served as Director of the Secretariat; they requested purchase of books from throughout the realm, selected descendants of fifth rank and above skilled at writing as copyists, transcribed and stored them in the inner repository, and had palace women keep charge of them.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenguan, Wei Zheng, Yu Shinan, and Yan Shigu served in turn as Director of the Secretariat; they petitioned to buy books empire-wide, appointed skilled copyists from families of fifth rank and above, transcribed the texts for the inner treasury, and entrusted them to palace women.

sentences.zh: 玄宗命左散騎常侍、昭文館學士馬懷素為脩圖書使，與右散騎常侍、崇文館學士褚無量整比。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong appointed Left Regular Attendant and Zhaowen Hall academician Ma Huaisu as Commissioner for Repairing the Library, together with Right Regular Attendant and Chongwen Hall academician Chu Wuliang to collate and arrange them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong named Left Regular Attendant and Zhaowen Hall scholar Ma Huaisu Commissioner for Repairing the Library, and paired him with Right Regular Attendant and Chongwen Hall scholar Chu Wuliang to collate the collection.

sentences.zh: 會幸東都，乃就乾元殿東序檢校。

translations.literal: When he happened to visit the eastern capital, they thereupon carried out inspection and collation in the eastern wing of the Qianyuan Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited the eastern capital, collation was carried out in the east wing of the Qianyuan Hall.

sentences.zh: 無量建議：禦書以宰相宋璟、蘇颋同署，如貞觀故事。

translations.literal: Wuliang proposed: imperial books should bear the joint signature of chief ministers Song Jing and Su Ting, following the Zhenguan precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Wuliang proposed that imperial books bear the joint attestation of chief ministers Song Jing and Su Ting, as in the Zhenguan precedent.

translations.literal: They also borrowed variant copies from among the people to transcribe.
translations.idiomatic: They also borrowed variant editions from private collections for copying.

sentences.zh: 及還京師，遷書東宮麗正殿，置修書院於著作院。

translations.literal: When they returned to the capital, they moved the books to the Lizheng Hall of the Eastern Palace and established the Academy for Repairing Books at the Composition Institute.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to the capital they moved the books to the Lizheng Hall in the Eastern Palace and set up the Academy for Repairing Books within the Composition Institute.

sentences.zh: 其後大明宮光順門外、東都明福門外，皆創集賢書院，學士通籍出入。

translations.literal: Afterward outside the Guangshun Gate of the Daming Palace and outside the Mingfu Gate of the eastern capital they each founded the Jixian Academy for Books, and academicians with registry passes came and went.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Jixian Academy was founded outside the Guangshun Gate of the Daming Palace and outside the Mingfu Gate at the eastern capital; scholars with registry passes entered freely.

sentences.zh: 既而太府月給蜀郡麻紙五千番，季給上谷墨三百三十六丸，歲給河間、景城、清河、博平四郡兔千五百皮為筆材。

translations.literal: Soon the Imperial Storehouse monthly supplied 5,000 sheets of hemp paper from Shu commandery, each quarter supplied 336 cakes of ink from Shanggu, and each year supplied 1,500 rabbit pelts from the four commanderies of Hejian, Jingcheng, Qinghe, and Boping as brush materials.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Storehouse then supplied 5,000 sheets of Shu hemp paper monthly, 336 cakes of Shanggu ink each quarter, and 1,500 rabbit pelts yearly from Hejian, Jingcheng, Qinghe, and Boping for brush-making.

sentences.zh: 兩都各聚書四部，以甲、乙、丙、丁為次，列經、史、子、集四庫。

translations.literal: The two capitals each gathered books in four divisions, using jia, yi, bing, and ding as the order, arraying the four repositories of Classics, Histories, Masters, and Collections.
translations.idiomatic: Each capital assembled books in four divisions, ranked jia through ding, in the four repositories of Classics, Histories, Masters, and Collections.

sentences.zh: 其本有正有副，軸帶帙簽皆異色以別之。

translations.literal: The exemplars had principal and duplicate copies; rollers, cords, wrappers, and labels were all in different colors to distinguish them.
translations.idiomatic: Each title had master and duplicate copies; rollers, ties, wrappers, and labels were color-coded to tell them apart.

translations.literal: In the rebellion of An Lushan, not a foot of bamboo slip was preserved.
translations.idiomatic: In An Lushan's rebellion scarcely a single scroll was saved.

sentences.zh: 元載為相，奏以千錢購書一卷，又命拾遺苗發等使江淮括訪。

translations.literal: When Yuan Zai was chief minister, he memorialized to purchase one scroll of books for a thousand cash, and also ordered Reminder Miao Fa and others to search and visit the Jiang-Huai region.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister Yuan Zai petitioned to pay a thousand cash per scroll for books and sent Reminder Miao Fa and others to search the Jiang-Huai region.

sentences.zh: 至文宗時，鄭覃侍講，進言經籍未備，因詔秘閣搜采，於是四庫之書復完，分藏於十二庫。

translations.literal: By the time of Emperor Wenzong, Zheng Tan lectured at court and advanced the statement that the classics and records were not complete; thereupon an edict ordered the Secret Archive to search and collect, and then the books of the four repositories were restored to completeness and divided for storage in twelve repositories.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wenzong, Zheng Tan, lecturing at court, reported that the canon was incomplete; the Secret Archive was ordered to search and collect, the four repositories were made whole again, and the books were divided among twelve storehouses.

translations.literal: In the turmoil of Huang Chao, those that survived were scarce indeed.
translations.idiomatic: After Huang Chao's rebellion, little survived.

sentences.zh: 昭宗播遷，京城制置使孫惟晟斂書本軍，寓教坊於秘閣，有詔還其書，命監察御史韋昌範等諸道求購，及徙洛陽，蕩然無遺矣。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong was driven into exile, Capital Arrangement Commissioner Sun Weicheng gathered books into his own army, lodged the Music Office in the Secret Archive; there was an edict to return the books, and Investigating Censor Wei Changfan and others were ordered to seek and purchase in the various circuits; when the court moved to Luoyang, nothing remained at all.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaozong fled the capital, Capital Arrangement Commissioner Sun Weicheng seized the books for his troops and quartered the Music Office in the Secret Archive; though an edict ordered the books returned and Investigating Censor Wei Changfan and others were sent to buy books throughout the circuits, by the time the court moved to Luoyang nothing was left.

sentences.zh: 甲部經錄，其類十一：一曰《易》類，二曰《書》類，三曰《詩》類，四曰《禮》類，五曰《樂》類，六曰《春秋》類，七曰《孝經》類，八曰《論語》類，九曰讖緯類，十曰經解類，十一曰小學類。

translations.literal: Section A, the record of Classics: its categories are eleven—first, the category of Changes; second, Documents; third, Odes; fourth, Rites; fifth, Music; sixth, Spring and Autumn; seventh, Filial Piety; eighth, Analects; ninth, prognostications and weft texts; tenth, classic exegesis; eleventh, philology.
translations.idiomatic: Section A, Classics: eleven categories—the Book of Changes, Documents, Odes, Rites, Music, Spring and Autumn, Filial Piety, Analects, prognostications and weft texts, classic exegesis, and philology.

sentences.zh: 凡著錄四百四十家，五百九十七部，六千一百四十五卷。

translations.literal: In all, entered in the catalog: 440 authors, 597 titles, 6,145 scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Catalogued in all: 440 authors, 597 titles, 6,145 scrolls.

sentences.zh: 不著錄一百一十七家，三千三百六十卷。

translations.literal: Not entered in the catalog: 117 authors, 3,360 scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Not catalogued: 117 authors, 3,360 scrolls.
